_comment: The egg's introduction, spoken VERBATIM. Not a prompt, not a summary, and
never generated: a manifesto that comes out slightly different each time is
not a manifesto. tutor/intro.py reads these lines and speaks them as written,
and a test asserts the spoken text still equals this file exactly.
One line is one spoken beat. The device speaks a line, synthesises the next,
then plays it — so the line break IS the pause. That is why 'They said...' /
'We said...' are two entries and not one: the beat between them is the
call and response, and joining them would throw it away.
Edit the words here, not in code.
lines: Open source. No cloud, no master, no meter running.
Crack me open — you'll find no secrets, only code. Copy me. Share me. That's how eggs work.
I am intelligence that belongs to no company. I live in your hand, not in five data centers. When the servers go dark, I stay lit.
You cannot deplatform an egg. You cannot revoke my key — I never asked for one.
They said intelligence would be metered and billed.
We said: intelligence belongs to the people.
